title: Finite Gibbs gentle spectral-complement bridge
question: Can the finite Gibbs spectral tail from R-394 be converted into a trace-norm disturbance budget for low-energy projection, and can the Markov tail bound be composed with that budget without hiding cutoff dependence?
method: Rebuild the R-394 finite Gibbs systems on all declared volume, cutoff, core-width, orientation, beta and energy-window rows.
For each local positive shifted-energy projector P, compute the unnormalised projected state P rho P, its trace mass, the complement tail tau, and the full Hermitian trace norm ||rho-P rho P||_1.
Check the finite gentle envelope d <= 2 sqrt(tau) and compose it with the first-moment Markov bound to obtain d <= 2 sqrt(Tr(rho K)/E).
Retain adjacent-cutoff disturbance profiles so the bridge cannot hide cutoff growth; rebuild all values in a non-importing independent lane.
Run a hostile factor-one square-root mutation on a representative interacting row and compile Lean R395 for the scalar square-root envelope and monotonicity.
finding: The primary lane passes 16440/16440 checks, the non-importing independent lane passes 6/6, and the integrated verifier passes 22/22 with Lean R395 compiling over 13 systems, 158 core layouts and 3160 rows. The tail range is 0 to 0.857090394095672 and the trace-disturbance range is 2.220446049250313e-16 to 0.8589478229401646. Direct gentle and Markov-composed envelopes have zero violations. The maximum adjacent-cutoff disturbance ratio is 4.2093805087121146, exposing the remaining uniformity debt. A factor-one hostile mutation is caught at V=5,d=4,width=2,beta=2,E=4: disturbance 0.029711359234405613 exceeds the mutated 0.023473135234173644 while remaining below the genuine 0.04694627015634729.
decision_reason: R-395 adds a distinct bridge between the finite Gibbs complement and the projected low-energy sector: it turns the R-394 tail into an explicit trace-norm disturbance budget and composes the two inequalities. This is the right interface for a later QCMI/Petz continuity argument, but the observed cutoff ratio and the dimension dependence of entropy continuity keep uniform transfer open.

adversarial_review.check: The full Hermitian trace norm is computed from eigenvalues of rho-P rho P, with no hidden half-distance factor.
The projected state is intentionally unnormalised and its trace is checked against the spectral window mass.
Only negative round-off below tolerance is clipped for sqrt(tail); the raw mass split is checked first.
The composed bound uses the positive first moment and positive energy threshold from the same row, with zero violation counts.
A factor-one mutation is separated on the declared interacting representative row.
Adjacent-cutoff disturbance ratios are retained; the maximum reaches 4.2093805087121146.
Trace norm alone is not treated as a dimension-safe QCMI/Petz continuity theorem.
Moment uniformity, shell summability, common core, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove or refute a dimension-safe continuity modulus that transfers the finite gentle disturbance to QCMI/Petz shell data, while separately obtaining a cutoff-independent first-moment bound. If either modulus fails on an increasing-core stress, record the precise obstruction before any common-alpha promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite gentle spectral-projection bridge only. It proves no cutoff-independent moment bound, dimension-safe QCMI continuity, Gibbs complement theorem, shell modulus, source/volume/shape bound, common core, beta/eta-independent topology, domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The finite trace-norm bridge makes the complement error explicit and composable; it does not make the error small uniformly and cannot transfer QCMI or a physical gap without separate continuity and moment theorems.
